name: BC-Z
summary: BC-Z collected over 25k demonstrations across 100 manipulation tasks using an interactive DAgger-style correction loop, and conditioned a single policy on either a language embedding or a human video of the task. It achieved meaningful zero-shot success on held-out tasks, establishing that task conditioning plus data diversity, rather than architecture, was the lever for generalization.
innovation: Task embeddings from language or video as the conditioning interface for a multi-task policy.
Shared-autonomy collection where humans correct the policy live, scaling data cheaply.
matters: The immediate methodological ancestor of RT-1 and the language-conditioned policy line.
limits: Zero-shot success rates were modest; generalization was narrow semantic interpolation.
lineage: Scaled, task-conditioned behavior cloning with DAgger-style corrections.
